title: ScreenR Example Analysis
text: R package ScreenR developed perform analysis High-throughput RNA interference screening using pooled shRNA libraries next generation sequencing.. Nowadays several short hairpin RNA (shRNA) libraries commercial available, last years interest type analysis, often called barcode screening, greatly increased benefits time-consuming point view possibility carrying screening large number genes simultaneously. However, bioinformatic analysis type screening still lacks golden standard. , ScreenR allows user carry preliminary quality check experiment, visually inspect data finally identify significant hits experiment series plots cross-statistical analyses. vignette gives overview whole analysis. step explained detail three tutorials: Getting data ScreenR: input tables, creation ScreenR object preparation data. Quality control: check screen worked. Finding validating hits: statistical methods, combine check candidate genes.

title: ScreenR Example Analysis
text: ScreenR considers final hit one result candidate hit three statistical methods. However particularly stringent method cases leads small number results. reason user can also decide opt less stringent method considers hits present least two statistical methods. two different strategies can computed function:: common_hit_TRT_at_least_2: considering candidate Hits one present least two three methods (less stringent) common_hit_TRT_at_least_3: considering candidate Hits one present three methods
code: common_hit_TRT_at_least_2 <- list(     Time3 = find_common_hit(         zscore_hit_TRT$Time3, camera_hit_TRT$Time3, roast_hit_TRT$Time3,         common_in = 2     ),     Time4 = find_common_hit(         zscore_hit_TRT$Time4, camera_hit_TRT$Time4, roast_hit_TRT$Time4,         common_in = 2     ) )  common_hit_TRT_at_least_3 <- list(     Time3 = find_common_hit(         zscore_hit_TRT$Time3, camera_hit_TRT$Time3, roast_hit_TRT$Time3,         common_in = 3     ),     Time4 = find_common_hit(         zscore_hit_TRT$Time4, camera_hit_TRT$Time4, roast_hit_TRT$Time4,         common_in = 3     ) )

title: Benchmark against MAGeCK and other tools
text: vignette compares hit-finding methods ScreenR tools pooled screens: MAGeCK RRA MAGeCK MLE (Li et al. 2014, 2015), used tools; BAGEL2 (Kim Hart 2021), supervised classifier essential genes; gscreend (Imkeller et al. 2020), Bioconductor package CRISPR screens; two plain edgeR/limma workflows: edgeR quasi-likelihood test counts summed gene, limma-voom camera barcodes gene (proposed shRNA CRISPR screens Dai et al. 2014). comparisons use simulated screens, true hits known exactly; published K562 shRNA essentiality screen (k562_count_table), core essential genes true hits non-essential genes true negatives; published HAP1 CRISPR-Cas9 essentiality screen, evaluated way; ScreenR example dataset (count_table), ground truth. tools Python programs packages dependencies ScreenR, results (MAGeCK 0.5.9.5, BAGEL2, gscreend 1.17.2, edgeR 4.0, limma 3.58) simulation results precomputed distributed inst/extdata/benchmark. ScreenR methods K562 screen run , vignette also shows compare ScreenR tools data. scripts produced precomputed results benchmark folder GitHub repository. differences tools run matter interpretation: BAGEL2 supervised: needs genes known essential non-essential train classifier. simulations trained half true hits half genes without effect, real screens reference genes used evaluation (10-fold cross-validation, standard use). reports Bayes factors, p-values, null calibration calls use FDR estimate. MAGeCK MLE p-values computed Wald statistic (pnorm(z), Benjamini-Hochberg), permutation FDR. gscreend accepts single reference sample, control replicates summed. deprecated Bioconductor 3.19.
code: library(ScreenR) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(ggplot2) benchmark_dir <- system.file("extdata", "benchmark", package = "ScreenR") labels <- c(     ScreenR_Zscore_mean = "ScreenR Z-score (mean)",     ScreenR_Zscore_edgeR = "ScreenR Z-score (edgeR)",     ScreenR_CAMERA = "ScreenR CAMERA",     ScreenR_FRY = "ScreenR FRY",     ScreenR_ROAST = "ScreenR ROAST",     ScreenR_Zscore_median = "ScreenR Z-score (median)",     ScreenR_Zscore_controls = "ScreenR Z-score (controls)",     ScreenR_CAMERA_storey = "ScreenR CAMERA (Storey)",     ScreenR_legacy_rule = "ScreenR legacy rule",     MAGeCK_RRA = "MAGeCK RRA",     MAGeCK_RRA_controls = "MAGeCK RRA (controls)",     MAGeCK_MLE = "MAGeCK MLE",     BAGEL2 = "BAGEL2",     gscreend = "gscreend",     edgeR_gene_QL = "edgeR gene-level QL",     limma_voom_camera = "limma-voom + camera" ) colours <- c(     "ScreenR Z-score (mean)" = "#1F5F55", "ScreenR Z-score (edgeR)" = "#93B5A3",     "ScreenR CAMERA" = "#2E8B7A", "ScreenR FRY" = "#C8DCD0",     "ScreenR ROAST" = "#7FBF7B", "ScreenR Z-score (median)" = "#4D9078",     "ScreenR Z-score (controls)" = "#B8E0D2",     "ScreenR CAMERA (Storey)" = "#5FA89A", "ScreenR legacy rule" = "grey50",     "MAGeCK RRA" = "#E3A894", "MAGeCK RRA (controls)" = "#F2CDBF",     "MAGeCK MLE" = "#B5523A", "BAGEL2" = "#5B4E9E", "gscreend" = "#D4A72C",     "edgeR gene-level QL" = "#4C78A8", "limma-voom + camera" = "#9ECAE9" ) # The methods shown in the figures (all methods are in the tables) main <- c("ScreenR_Zscore_mean", "ScreenR_Zscore_edgeR", "ScreenR_CAMERA",     "ScreenR_FRY", "MAGeCK_RRA", "MAGeCK_MLE", "BAGEL2", "gscreend",     "edgeR_gene_QL", "limma_voom_camera") scenarios <- c(     S0_null = "No hits", S1_baseline = "Baseline",     S2_weak_effect = "Weak effect", S3_two_replicates = "2 replicates",     S4_noisy = "Noisy", S5_off_target = "Off-target" )

code: evaluate <- function(result, alpha = 0.05) {     # Genes are sorted by name, so that tied p-values are ordered the same     # way for every method     merged <- left_join(k562_reference_genes, result, by = "Gene") %>%         mutate(PValue = coalesce(PValue, 1), FDR = coalesce(FDR, 1)) %>%         arrange(Gene)     essential <- merged$Class == "core essential"     called <- merged$FDR <= alpha     hit <- essential[order(merged$PValue)]     precision <- cumsum(hit) / seq_along(hit)     tibble(         `Essential called` = sum(called & essential),         `Non-essential called` = title: Choosing the reference of the gene-level test
text: find_gene_zscore_hit() decides whether gene hit comparing score reference: score gene without effect looks like. Two references available: reference = "random" (default): random sets barcodes, drawn barcodes control_genes; reference = "empirical": empirical null, distribution scores genes without effect estimated data. suggest reference = "empirical" libraries hundreds genes , without effect, case genome-wide focused screens: random barcodes two problems, shown screens distributed ScreenR: dropout screens hits make conservative (many hits missed), shRNA screens give p-values small (genes without effect called). empirical null neither problem. default still "random", results existing analyses change. Always look plot_empirical_null() (see Checking fit).

title: Choosing the reference of the gene-level test
text: gene gets score, mean Z-scores barcodes (see Tutorial 3). hit gene whose score extreme scores genes without effect, test needs know scores distributed. random barcodes, score gene k barcodes compared scores many random sets k barcodes. assumes barcodes gene without effect behave like barcodes taken random reference. empirical null, score gene standardized statistic (centred median barcode scores divided median absolute deviation k\sqrt{k}). genes effect, centre distribution statistics made genes without effect: normal distribution fitted , p-value gene comes . hits, tail, left fit. Two fits available: empirical_fit = "central" (default): parabola fitted log density statistics around mode (central matching, Efron’s locfdr); empirical_fit = "one-sided": centre mode spread estimated side without hits (mode depleted genes, direction = "").

title: Choosing the reference of the gene-level test
text: core essential non-essential genes Hart et al. give answer: essential genes hits, non-essential genes . Half non-essential genes used control_genes (best possible reference, genes known); half kept every reference, count false calls. columns tables number genes called 5% FDR (Called), share core essential genes among (Essential found), number held-non-essential genes called (NE called) share held-non-essential genes p-value 0.05 (NE p <= 0.05). last one check p-values: genes effect, 5% p-value 0.05. Much less means conservative test (hits missed), much means p-values small (genes without effect called).
code: data(hart_reference_genes) essential <- hart_reference_genes$Gene[     hart_reference_genes$Class == "core essential"] nonessential <- hart_reference_genes$Gene[     hart_reference_genes$Class == "non-essential"] set.seed(2017) reference <- sample(nonessential, length(nonessential) %/% 2) held_out <- setdiff(nonessential, reference)  evaluate <- function(result) {     called <- result$Gene[result$FDR <= 0.05]     tested_null <- result$Gene %in% held_out     data.frame(         Called = length(called),         `Essential found` = mean(essential[essential %in% result$Gene]             %in% called),         `NE called` = sum(called %in% held_out),         `NE p <= 0.05` = mean(result$PValue[tested_null] <= 0.05),         check.names = FALSE     ) }

text: edgeR/limma based methods need design matrix contrast. common pitfall rename columns model.matrix(~ groups): model.matrix() orders columns alphabetically group first group becomes intercept, renaming another order silently compares wrong samples. create_design_matrix() creates design matrix one column group (intercept) create_contrast() creates comparison groups name, avoids problem.

text: methods use replicates fit linear model, needs two things: design matrix, says group sample belongs ; contrast, says groups compare. create_design_matrix() builds design matrix groups object: one column per group, 1 column group sample. title: Tutorial 3: Finding and validating hits
text: methods test barcodes gene set, edgeR raw counts normalization object. FRY ROAST ask whether barcodes gene change (self-contained test). ROAST uses random rotations: set seed get result every time use many rotations (nrot, default 9999) real analysis; 999 keep tutorial fast. FRY (method = "fry") computes test exactly, without rotations: faster, p-values limited number rotations, recommended choice. CAMERA asks whether barcodes gene change barcodes (competitive test), taking account correlation barcodes. two kinds tests answer different questions. self-contained test calls gene barcodes depleted replicates vary, even many genes depleted; competitive test calls stands rest library, becomes conservative many genes effect. hand FRY ROAST rely variability replicates: need replicates groups, little power two replicates noisy data, find almost nothing control single sample (example plasmid library). p-values one-sided, requested direction. number_barcode sets minimum number barcodes (number_barcode) gene needs tested, direction chooses depleted ("") enriched ("") genes. Use PValue FDR: “Mixed” columns test whether barcodes change direction, also call genes whose barcodes disagree.

title: Tutorial 3: Finding and validating hits
text: find_gene_zscore_hit() computes gene mean Z-score barcodes (statistic = "median" uses median, less affected single barcode strong, possibly -target, effect) compares reference distribution: reference = "random" (default): scores random sets barcodes size, drawn n_permutations times (seed makes reproducible). control_genes random sets drawn control genes instead. controls behave like genes without effect: non-targeting shRNAs often (targeting shRNAs usually somewhat depleted compared , every gene looks depleted). reference = "empirical": distribution scores genes without effect, estimated centre distribution genes. accounts barcodes gene varying together, makes random sets give small p-values, especially shRNA screens. needs library hundreds genes, without effect (see empirical null vignette). plot_empirical_null() shows gene scores fitted null, follow centre distribution:  null almost standard normal (mean 0.01, standard deviation 1), long tail depleted genes: treatment effect moderate concerns genes.

ScreenR reimplement method: calls CRISPRcleanR. correction needs complete genome-wide library: CRISPRcleanR assumes genes region effect. subset genes enriched hits removes real signal, must used hap1_count_table; library annotation position sgRNA, format CRISPRcleanR (row names: sgRNA identifiers; columns GENES, CHRM, STARTpos ENDpos). code: zscore_default <- find_gene_zscore_hit(statistics, fdr = 1, seed = 1) camera <- find_camera_hit(object, design, contrast,     number_barcode = 2, fdr = 1 ) fry <- find_roast_hit(object, design, contrast,     method = "fry", number_barcode = 2, fdr = 1 ) hit_list <- list(zscore_reference = zscore,     zscore_empirical = zscore_empirical,     zscore_one_sided = zscore_one_sided, zscore = zscore_default,     camera = camera, fry = fry) hits <- summarise_hits(hit_list, fdr = 0.05) head(hits) #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   Gene    FDR_zscore_reference FDR_zscore_empirical FDR_zscore_one_sided #>   <chr>                  <dbl>                <dbl>                <dbl> #> 1 ATP6V1F            0.0000476         0.0000000236             4.47e-14 #> 2 BUB3               0.0000476         0.0000000130             1.47e-14 #> 3 CPSF1              0.0000476         0.0000000345             9.08e-14 #> 4 DHX15              0.0000476         0.0000000102             8.10e-15 #> 5 DPAGT1             0.0000476         0.0000000262             5.44e-14 #> 6 EIF3A              0.0000476         0.0000000101             6.35e-15 #> # ℹ 6 more variables: FDR_zscore <dbl>, FDR_camera <dbl>, FDR_fry <dbl>, #> #   NMethods <dbl>, MaxFDR <dbl>, Hit <lgl> table(hits$NMethods) #>  #>    0    1    2    3    4    5    6  #> 2415   22   98  121  294   69  332 plot_common_hit(hit_list, fdr = 0.05,     title = "Depleted genes at day 18 (5% FDR)") evaluate_hits <- function(result) {     called <- result$Gene[result$FDR <= 0.05]     data.frame(         `Genes called` = length(called),         `Core essential` = sum(called %in% essential),         `Held-out non-essential` = sum(called %in% held_out),         check.names = FALSE     ) } knitr::kable(bind_rows(lapply(hit_list, evaluate_hits), .id = "Method"))

Compare treated control cells last time point two independent tests, combine : Look barcodes top candidate trusting :
code: library(ScreenR) data(count_table) data(annotation_table) counts <- count_table[count_table$Barcode != "*", ] colnames(counts) <- c(     "Barcode", "Time1", "Time2", "Time3_TRT_A", "Time3_TRT_B", "Time3_TRT_C",     "Time3_CTRL_A", "Time3_CTRL_B", "Time3_CTRL_C",     "Time4_TRT_A", "Time4_TRT_B", "Time4_TRT_C",     "Time4_CTRL_A", "Time4_CTRL_B", "Time4_CTRL_C" ) groups <- factor(c(     "T1/T2", "T1/T2", rep("Time3_TRT", 3), rep("Time3_CTRL", 3),     rep("Time4_TRT", 3), rep("Time4_CTRL", 3) ))  # 1. Create the object and normalize the counts object <- create_screenr_object(     table = counts, annotation = annotation_table, groups = groups ) object <- compute_data_table(normalize_data(remove_all_zero_row(object))) object #> class: screenr_object  #> dim: 5317 14  #> metadata(0): #> assays(2): counts normalized #> rownames(5317): 10208 10502 ... 13876 13995 #> rowData names(5): Barcode Gene Gene_ID Sequence Library #> colnames(14): Time1 Time2 ... Time4_CTRL_B Time4_CTRL_C #> colData names(4): Sample Day Treatment Group #> data table: 74438 rows, 9 columns plot_mds(object) + ggplot2::theme_bw() # 2. Define the comparison design <- create_design_matrix(object) contrast <- create_contrast(design, treatment = "Time4_TRT", control = "Time4_CTRL")  # 3. Gene-level permutation test on replicate-aware barcode statistics barcode_statistics <- compute_barcode_statistics(object, design, contrast) zscore <- find_gene_zscore_hit(barcode_statistics, fdr = 1, seed = 1)  # 4. limma CAMERA on the barcodes of each gene camera <- find_camera_hit(object, design, contrast, fdr = 1)  # 5. One table with the FDR of both methods, best supported genes first #    (the example screen has a weak effect, so we use a lenient FDR of 25%) hits <- summarise_hits(list(zscore = zscore, camera = camera), fdr = 0.25) head(hits) #> # A tibble: 6 x 6 #>   Gene     FDR_zscore FDR_camera NMethods MaxFDR Hit   #>   <chr>         <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl> <lgl> #> 1 Gene_173      0.128     0.0882        2  0.128 TRUE  #> 2 Gene_422      0.187     0.0882        2  0.187 TRUE  #> 3 Gene_15       0.233     0.232         2  0.233 TRUE  #> 4 Gene_296      0.250     0.0882        2  0.250 TRUE  #> 5 Gene_370      0.280     0.232         1  0.280 FALSE #> 6 Gene_352      0.280     0.232         1  0.280 FALSE top_gene <- as.character(hits$Gene[1]) plot_boxplot(object,     genes = top_gene, group_var = c("TRT", "CTRL"), fill_var = "Treatment" ) +     ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(CTRL = "#93B5A3", TRT = "#C9836A")) +     ggplot2::theme_bw() +     ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

text: Iorio F, Behan FM, Goncalves E, et al. (2018). Unsupervised     correction gene-independent cell responses CRISPR-Cas9     targeting. BMC Genomics 19:604. doi:10.1186/s12864-018-4989-y

title: Correct CRISPR-Cas9 copy-number and proximity bias with CRISPRcleanR — correct_crispr_bias
code: # Needs the CRISPRcleanR package, which is not on CRAN or Bioconductor: # BiocManager::install("francescojm/CRISPRcleanR") if (crisprcleanr_available()) {     ccr <- "CRISPRcleanR"     # The KY library annotation distributed with CRISPRcleanR     KY_Library_v1.0 <- get(utils::data("KY_Library_v1.0", package = ccr))     file <- system.file("extdata", "HT-29_counts.tsv", package = ccr)     counts <- read.delim(file)     # A few chromosomes to keep the example fast     keep <- KY_Library_v1.0[counts$sgRNA, "CHRM"] %in% c("8", "17")     counts <- counts[keep, ]     colnames(counts) <- c("Barcode", "Gene", "Plasmid", "R1", "R2", "R3")     object <- create_screenr_object(         table = counts[, -2],         annotation = counts[, c("Barcode", "Gene")],         groups = factor(c("Plasmid", "Late", "Late", "Late")),         sample_table = data.frame(             Sample = c("Plasmid", "R1", "R2", "R3"), Day = "Screen",             Treatment = c("Plasmid", "Late", "Late", "Late")         )     )     corrected <- correct_crispr_bias(object,         library_annotation = KY_Library_v1.0,         control = "Plasmid", treatment = c("R1", "R2", "R3")     )     corrected }

title: ScreenR 1.15.16
text: Tutorial 3 (finding validating hits) uses current functions: sample table palettes creation, theme_set(), TMM normalization, FRY recommended test, empirical null, plot_common_hit() number methods (UpSet plot), find_consistent_hit(), find_time_hit() real times, plot_trend(color_by = ), plot_treatment_separation() plot_barcode_heatmap() check candidates. Tutorial 4 (CRISPR-Cas9 screens) uses palettes, theme_set(), trend reference genes real days, sgRNAs plot_barcode_heatmap(), overlap methods plot_common_hit(), explains baseline normalization affects self-contained tests. plot_treatment_separation() plots descriptive treatment/control abundance ratios two condition labels configurable time metadata. retains selected stages, supports real times sample subsets, inherits user theme. Missing comparisons never assigned zero effects. plot_trend(color_by = "Treatment") overlays separate condition trends biological sample points lines joining time-point means. original ungrouped regression remains default without color_by; trend = "lm" explicitly fits separate regressions. Object palettes used, reference_groups shows shared baselines neutral points. connect_reference joins shared reference history condition means; highlight_difference shades observed gap two conditions. theme applied new plots; use theme_set() user code. plot_barcode_heatmap() shows individual barcode abundances across samples, gene sample-variable panels. Display log2 normalized counts, barcode-centered values values relative explicit reference samples. Model designs now carry sample identifiers checked object fitting. Custom designs must sample identifiers row names object order. Named contrast vectors one-column contrast matrices aligned coefficient names; missing, duplicated unknown names rejected. Unnamed numeric contrast vectors remain positional. Package checks, coverage website builds now run pushes pull requests devel. Website builds devel deploy GitHub Pages. find_consistent_hit() tests directional effects shared supplied contrasts using FRY, ROAST, CAMERA gene-level Z-scores (random empirical reference). combine_consistent_hits() accepts complete one-sided gene-level p-value tables, combines raw p-values intersection-union test applies BH correction across genes.
